memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then Caleb silenced the people before Moses and said, "We should go up and take possession of the land, for we can certainly do it." — Num 13:30 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
In the middle of a frightened crowd, one voice rings out with courage. Caleb quiets the murmuring and says plainly, "We should go up and take possession of the land, for we can certainly do it." He had seen exactly what the others saw — the giants, the walls, the powerful people. But he saw them through different eyes.

What made Caleb different? Not that he underestimated the enemy. He knew the giants were real. The difference was that Caleb factored God into the equation. "We can certainly do it" was not confidence in Israel's military strength; it was confidence in the God who had promised the land. Caleb was not being naive; he was being faithful.

It often takes just one person of faith to stand against the tide of fear. Caleb did not wait for the majority to agree with him. He spoke up alone, willing to be the lone voice of confidence in a sea of anxiety. Faith sometimes means standing by yourself when everyone around you has given in to fear.

Are you willing to be the Caleb in your family, your workplace, your church — the one who says, "With God, we can," when everyone else is saying, "We can't"? It is not always comfortable. But God notices such faith. As we will later read, Caleb's trust would be richly honoured. The One who calls us forward is faithful, and He is worth trusting even when we stand alone.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you willing to be a lone voice of faith when others give in to fear?
2. What made Caleb see the same situation so differently from the others?
3. Where do you need to declare "with God, we can" today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, give me the faith of Caleb — to trust You even when I stand alone. Help me to factor You into every situation and to be a voice of courage when others are gripped by fear. Amen.
